name: Cisplatin radiosensitizer with concurrent radiation (bladder trimodality)
cyclesNote: Radiosensitizing cisplatin given concurrently with the external-beam radiation course of bladder-preserving trimodality therapy. Common schedules: cisplatin weekly during RT, or every 3 weeks; the number of doses tracks the radiation schedule.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Concurrent cisplatin is a radiosensitizer during bladder-preserving trimodality therapy (maximal TURBT + chemoradiation) for selected muscle-invasive disease. Requires adequate renal function; not interchangeable with carboplatin in this curative setting.

premedications.name: Hydration + antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: Pre- and post-cisplatin IV hydration and highly-emetogenic antiemetic prophylaxis on chemotherapy days.

supportiveCare: Aggressive IV hydration with cisplatin to protect renal function; monitor magnesium/potassium and replete.
Coordinate chemotherapy days with the radiation schedule; deliver on radiation-treatment days.
Restaging cystoscopy + biopsy after chemoradiation to confirm response; salvage cystectomy for non-response.
monitoring: renal function and electrolytes (Mg, K) before each dose
radiation cystitis / proctitis during the course

doseModificationRules.condition: declining renal function or significant cytopenia during chemoradiation
doseModificationRules.text: Hold or reduce cisplatin for rising creatinine, electrolyte wasting, or myelosuppression; radiation generally continues. Physician decides.

drugs.name: CISplatin
drugs.notes: CISplatin 40 mg/m2 IV weekly concurrent with radiation (radiosensitizer). An alternative schedule is CISplatin 70 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks during RT. Requires hydration and adequate renal function; ISMP tall-man CISplatin (distinguish from CARBOplatin). Own wording; standard reference dose.

provenance.locator: Principles of bladder preservation - concurrent cisplatin radiosensitization
